overview: Suriname is the smallest country in South America. Its capital and largest city is Paramaribo. Suriname was a Dutch colony until 1975, and it is the only country in South America where Dutch is the official language. Its people have roots in many places, including Africa, India, Indonesia, China and Europe, as well as Indigenous peoples.

geography.text: Most people live along the narrow coastal plain. The rest of Suriname is covered by dense tropical rainforest, making it one of the most forested countries in the world, crossed by rivers flowing north to the Atlantic. The Brokopondo Reservoir, created by a dam in the 1960s, is one of the largest reservoirs in the world.

history.text: The Dutch took Suriname from the English in 1667, while the English kept New Amsterdam, later New York. Plantations were worked by enslaved Africans, many of whom escaped into the rainforest and formed free Maroon communities. After slavery ended in 1863, workers came from India and Java. Suriname became independent in 1975.

events.title: Treaty of Breda
events.text: The Dutch keep Suriname and the English keep New Amsterdam.

events.title: Slavery abolished
events.text: Slavery ends in the Dutch colonies.

events.title: Workers from India
events.text: The first indentured workers arrive from India.

government.text: Suriname is a republic in which the President is head of both state and government. The National Assembly elects the President. Suriname became independent from the Netherlands in 1975. In 2025 Jennifer Geerlings-Simons became its first female President.

economy.text: Gold and oil are Suriname's main exports, and major new offshore oil finds may change its economy. Bauxite mining was once the largest industry. More than 90% of the country is covered in rainforest.

culture.text: Suriname is the smallest country in South America and the only one where Dutch is the official language. Its people are among the most diverse in the world, with roots in India, Africa, Java, China and Indigenous and Maroon communities. Sranan Tongo is the common language on the street.

items.title: Paramaribo
items.text: A colonial capital of wooden buildings, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Rainforest
items.text: More than 90% of the country is covered in forest.

sport.text: Football is very popular, and many great Dutch players have Surinamese roots, including Clarence Seedorf and Ruud Gullit. Swimmer Anthony Nesty won Suriname's first Olympic gold in 1988.

items.text: Anthony Nesty won Olympic gold in the 100 m butterfly.

didYouKnow: More than 90% of Suriname is covered by forest, one of the highest shares in the world.
In Paramaribo, a mosque and a synagogue stand side by side.
